suggestions.assertion: No content is copied verbatim from the source beyond a short quoted phrase
suggestions.reason: This assertion is structurally unverifiable in the without_skill condition as currently run: the task tells the executor to synthesize its own 'source document' (since none was attached), and that synthesized source is written only to the executor's private scratchpad, never saved into outputs_dir or anywhere else the grader can reach. Without the source text, verbatim-overlap can never be checked either way — it will fail every run of this eval for lack of evidence, regardless of actual output quality. Consider requiring the harness to persist the synthesized source (e.g. to outputs/source-document.md or a fixed sibling location) so this assertion has something to compare against.

Both scripts/lint_skill.py and quick_validate.py expectations depend on tooling that is only available inside the skill-creator-pro skill, which this without_skill condition is explicitly instructed not to invoke. As written, these two expectations are guaranteed to fail on every without_skill run for a reason that has nothing to do with output quality (shape, budget, organization, fidelity all passed here). If the intent is to demonstrate that the baseline skips validation entirely, that's a valid and even useful differentiator to capture — but it's worth confirming the with_skill condition actually exercises both scripts, and considering whether these two belong in a separate 'validation' checklist that is scored/reported distinctly from the four structural/content expectations, so a reader doesn't read '3 of 7 failed' as a content-quality problem when it's actually a tooling-availability artifact of the condition.

eval_feedback.overall: The four structural/content expectations (shape, budget, topic organization, index accuracy) are all genuinely discriminating and all passed with strong, specific evidence — this looks like a solid without_skill run on those dimensions. The remaining three failures are not quality problems with the output; they reflect two evaluability gaps in the eval itself: (1) the verbatim-copying check has no ground truth to check against in this condition, and (2) the two validator-script checks are inherently unreachable without invoking the very skill this condition is designed to withhold. Recommend either fixing the harness to persist the synthesized source, or reclassifying/separating the two script-based expectations so their expected failure in without_skill doesn't read as a comparable content defect.
